synthesis: In logarithmic superdiffusion, the Gaussian core controls weak convergence while expanding ballistic tails remain visible at finite time and supply the part of the second moment not represented by that core; the source's tail-balance argument therefore predicts that the limiting Gaussian covariance Xi equals D rather than the normal-diffusion relation Xi=2D.
source_support: Unit u02 defines separately the second-moment tensor D and weak-limit covariance Xi and explains why weak convergence need not control moments with spreading heavy tails. Unit u03 records this distinction and its borderline second-moment status. Unit u04 provides simulation evidence of a Gaussian core coexisting with expanding ballistic tails. Unit u05 compares known coefficient formulas, obtains Xi=D in the square case, and heuristically splits the Green-Kubo integral so the core supplies half of the full logarithmic second moment, with rare long flights supplying the remainder.
nonparaphrase_operation: Reconciles apparently inconsistent covariance conventions by decomposing the finite-time distribution into a weak-limit core and a moment-dominating tail, identifying which statistic samples each region.
limits: This adjudication uses only the current local parent slices. The finite-time core/tail coexistence is numerical and the half-contribution calculation is explicitly heuristic, with lower-order logarithmic corrections suppressed. The arbitrary-dimensional extension is proposed rather than proved here, although cited two-dimensional formulas agree. Square-root scalings, matrix indices, coefficient normalizations, and tail-balance equations require PDF verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because four parents jointly support a concrete core-versus-tail mechanism and a calibrated coefficient prediction, with simulation and heuristic status preserved.

synthesis: For a non-incipient horizon of dimension d_H, the proved single-horizon calculation gives survival of order t^{-(d-d_H)}; Conjecture 1 promotes the finite sum over maximal horizons to the global survival law, and Conjecture 3 promotes collision-free constant-velocity contributions to the leading correlation. Consequently only principal horizons, with codimension one, yield the 1/t correlation scale that integrates to logarithmic superdiffusion.
source_support: Unit u06 defines horizons, their dimensions, and survival probabilities. Units u07-u08 state maximal-horizon dominance as Conjecture 1 and derive the conditional finite visibility-weighted sum. Unit u18 proves the t^{-(d-d_H)} contribution for one non-incipient horizon. Unit u10 states the post-collision decorrelation estimate as Conjecture 3. Unit u11 gives the superdiffusion matrix and survival-trace relation conditional on Conjectures 1 and 3.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes local geometric codimension scaling with two explicitly conjectural dominance/decorrelation reductions to identify the unique horizon dimension capable of producing a logarithmic Green-Kubo divergence.
limits: Only the single-horizon asymptotic is unconditional among the decisive decay steps. Global dominance is Conjecture 1, correlation reduction is Conjecture 3, and the matrix and trace relation inherit both; model-specific failures of the decorrelation heuristic are noted. Multi-line visibility integrals, matrix normalizations, and projection factors are formula-sensitive and require PDF checking.
quality_reason: Accepted because the parents support a precise local-exponent-to-global-correlation chain and clearly expose which links are lemmas, conditional theorems, and conjectures.

synthesis: Primitive dual vectors encode principal horizons; Mobius inversion removes primitivity and inserts a reciprocal Riemann-zeta factor into the Mellin representation. Formally shifting that contour then makes residues at zeta zeros govern the small-scatterer remainder, and the same horizon sum enters diffusivity through the survival-diffusion relation, carrying the formal RH-sensitive remainder to D.
source_support: Unit u19 identifies principal horizons with primitive dual-lattice vectors and writes the width-cutoff survival sum. Unit u21 applies Mobius inversion and Mellin transformation, producing an integrand with 1/zeta(s+1), while explicitly stating that the needed vanishing sequence of left contours is unproved. Unit u22 describes the resulting pole structure and conditionally states the RH-sized remainder, with numerical residue comparisons only. Unit u28 combines the survival relation with the diffusion theorem to reproduce the same formal remainder for cubic diffusivity.
nonparaphrase_operation: Transforms a geometric primitive-counting problem into an analytic pole problem and then transports its unresolved remainder through a separate survival-to-diffusion identity.
limits: The contour-closing step is not proved, so the residue expansion, RH-sized error, and suggested RH equivalence are not established results. The survival formula already depends on Conjecture 1, while diffusivity also depends on Conjecture 3; Epstein-zeta facts are cited. Mobius factors, Mellin arguments, lattice normalizations, threshold radii, and equations (27)-(31),(37)-(38) are highly OCR/formula-sensitive and require PDF verification.

synthesis: At the touching transition, an incipient principal horizon has zero direct measure but contains countably many codimension-two subordinate horizons. Rescaling their cross-sections yields an individual contribution proportional to 1/(t^2 L^5); summing over lattice directions converges through dimension five and diverges from dimension six, providing a geometric summability mechanism for a critical change in survival decay.
source_support: Unit u15 defines incipient horizons and proves that an incipient horizon of dimension greater than one contains countably many lower-dimensional horizon directions. Unit u24 derives the limiting parabolic cross-section, obtains an L^{-6} visibility integral and hence an L^{-5}/t^2 contribution, and identifies the Epstein-series convergence threshold d=6. Unit u09 states the resulting piecewise critical-dimension law as Conjecture 2. Unit u25 reports fitted finite-time exponents and emphasizes slow convergence and unknown high-dimensional asymptotics.
nonparaphrase_operation: Converts a zero-width dominant geometry into a lattice summability problem over subordinate modes and uses its convergence threshold to explain why dimension six is structurally special.
limits: The L^{-5} scaling and convergence threshold support a mechanism, but divergence alone proves neither the tentative t^{-2} log t law at d=6 nor the fractional exponents above six; those are conjectural and numerically supported only. The visibility constant is numerical, the order of limits matters, and overlaps among infinitely many horizons require further calculation. Formula (33)-(34), lattice normalizations, and fitted values need PDF verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because the parents jointly provide a concrete geometry-to-series transformation and a mathematically identified threshold, while all proposed time exponents remain correctly limited.
